The CT scan performed here showed benign cysts of liver and an incidental right renal mass. Specimen: Right renal tissue. Macro: A portion of renal tissue measuring 2.5x2x1.5cm. it contains a pale nodule measuring 1.5cm in maximum dimension with a uniformly pale cut surface and close to the re-section margin. Immuno: Positive for SMA and HMB45 and patchy positivity for Pan M (melanA/HMB45 cocktail).
casos.comentario: This was a case of angiomyolipoma correctly diagnosed by 100% of participants.

casos.clinica: Renal tumour. Specimen: Radical Nephrectomy. Macro: Dark brown tumour with some cystic change and haemorrhage 58mm maximum. Immuno: Positive for CD56, chromogranin and synaptophysin and vimentin. Negative for RENCA, CD10 , Ckit & CK7. Proliferation index Ki67 2-20/10hpf
casos.comentario: This was a rare tumour of the kidney but 73% correctly diagnosed this as a carcinoid. This did have some areas of nuclear pleomorphism and as a result neuroendocrine carcinoma was also felt to be correct as there is considerable overlap between these entities. Both these responses scored 1 point. All other diagnoses were considered incorrect.

casos.clinica: Asyptomatic lesion discovered on ultrasound scan. Right bladder wall lump above RUO - described on request card as "not typical of TCC". Specimen: Bladder biopsy. Macro: Pale tissue 8mm in maximum extent. Immuno: None.
casos.comentario: This was submitted as an unusual case of cystitis cystica and indeed 73% of participants called it this. There is considerable overlap between this and cystitis glandularis and as a result this was deemed to be correct as well. In areas the lining urothelium showed some hobnail change but this was considered by the meeting to represent umbrella cells rather than nephrogenic metaplasia, which was deemed to be incorrect as were the other diagnoses offered.

casos.clinica: New bladder tumour resected to muscle. Specimen: Bladder (TURBT). Macro: Chippings weighing 4g. Immuno: None.
casos.comentario:
This case had two parts which both received up to a maximum of 0.5 marks.
This was a case of transitional cell carcinoma with some lymphoepithelioma-like areas but no keratinisation was seen. There was insufficient agreement to score this case without joining response categories. It was felt that TCC, TCC lymphoepithelioma-like and TCC undifferentiated would all be treated similarly and this gained 1 mark but as there were no true areas of squamous differentiation then TCC with squamous differentiation was deemed to be worth half marks. There were no spindle cell areas so TCC sarcomatoid was deemed incorrect as were the other diagnoses. One person stated Other but their comments were deemed by the audience as incorrect as there was a category of TCC undifferentiated.
There was a supplementary question asking for stage and 98.6% stated pT2 and this scored full marks, whilst pT1 (1 person) and pTa (3 people) were deemed incorrect.

casos.clinica: Urethral lesion ?TCC. Specimen: Urethral biopsy. Macro: A light brown strip of tissue 35mm in length x up to 2mm in diameter and a second fragment 2mm diameter. Immuno: None.
casos.comentario: This case caused much debate and a member of the audience favoured a fibroepithelial polyp - which was not an available diagnosis but was mentioned by someone in the Other response category. There was over 70% agreement for inverted papilloma, so it was felt that this should be scored. The lesion did have an inverted growth pattern and it was felt that this and urothelial papilloma were correct and scored 1. A warning email had been circulated before this circulation warning participant's that they may score zero if the diagnosis they wanted was available but they put Other. The diagnoses (or synonyms of) listed by people putting Other were available apart from fibroepithelial polyp, so all these participants were deemed to score 0 apart from this person. Inverted urothelial papilloma was in the neoplastic category as the cancerous and non-|cancerous terms had been replaced for circulation L (see comments on K6). All other diagnoses were deemed incorrect.

casos.clinica: Known metastatic Ca breast. Bladder mass on CT. ?Extrinsic. Resection biopsy of mass done. Specimen: Transurethral resection of bladder tumour. Macro: Bladder tumour chippings aggregating 32mm. Immuno: ER pos. PR neg. E-cadherin pos.
casos.comentario: The history was of breast cancer and the cells showed Indian file growth pattern. This was a case of metastatic tumour. The participants stating other all listed metastatic breast carcinoma - it is clear that the drop down box system cannot list all types of primary and they should have put metastatic tumour and then added a comment but the meeting felt that they should receive full marks. Given the history this was the most likely working diagnosis and as a result all other diagnoses were deemed incorrect.

casos.clinica: Right renal hilar tumour in a solitary kidney. Specimen: Right partial nephrectomy/enucleation specimen. Macro: Partial nephrectomy specimen comprising a lobulated tumour with adjacent hilar fat. The tumour measures 45mm in maximum dimension and the cut surface has a diffuse mahogany brown appearance. It extends to the surgical margin in places. No background normal renal parenchyma is identified. Immuno: Scattered cells positive for CK7. Stong and diffuse staining for CD117. Patchy staining for CD10. Negative staining for RCC antigen and vimentin.
casos.comentario: This was a straightforward case of renal oncocytoma correctly diagnosed by 96.8% of participants and supported by the provided immuno profile (scattered cells positive for CK7, strong and diffuse staining for CD117. Patchy staining for CD10. Negative for RCC and vimentin). A number of people had commented on the presence of focal infiltration of fat which it was emphasised is an acceptable morphological feature in Oncocytoma. Category 2 was regarded incorrect and scored 0.

casos.clinica: Solid Tumour, right bladder wall,negative urine cytology. A bit atypical at TURBT. Specimen: Bladder chippings. Macro: 7 grams of bladder chippings. Immuno: N/A
casos.comentario: This case contained mixed Mullerian elements including endometriosis, endocervicosis and endosalpingosis. It was emphasised that by convention, the presence of two or more of these is best referred to as Mullerianosis which was correctly identified by 37% of participants. It was agreed that for scoring purposes categories 1, 2 & 3 should be merged and receive full marks and that the remaining categories 4-8 should be regarded incorrect and score 0.

casos.clinica: ?left cystic renal cancer. Specimen: Left Kidney. Macro: Well defined cystic lesion involving the lower 2/3 of kidney, containing clear serous fluid, measuring 13 x 10 x 6 cm. No solid areas. Immuno: N/A
casos.comentario: This was a case of cystic nephroma (CN) correctly diagnosed by 89.5% of participants. It was agreed that mixed epithelial stromal tumour (MEST) (believed by many to be ends of a spectrum with CN) and favoured by 5.6% of participants was also acceptable and should be merged for scoring purposes. It was indicated that renal epithelial stromal tumour (REST) had been proposed as an alternative term for these closely related tumours and drew attention to a comment stating that this was a rare tumour and questioning whether it was suitable for EQA. Interestingly, on a show of hands the majority of the audience had in fact diagnosed this tumour in their own practice. After a vote it was also agreed to merge category 6 'other (please state in comments below)' which one person had used (having put CN in the comments section). Categories 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9 & 10 were regarded incorrect and scored 0.

casos.clinica: Left pyonephrosis 10 weeks. Unwell, weight loss. Specimen: Radical Nephrectomy. Macro: A kidney with attached perinephric tissue weighing 274g. The kidney measures 74x50x35mm with attached perinephric fat up to 30 mm. Adrenal gland is not identified. The ureter appears to be cut almost flush to the periureteric junction. On bisection, renal pelvis is dilated to 52mm maximum dimension. Renal calyces and adjacent cortex show multiple soft yellowish areas suggestive of suppuration measuring up to 18mm maximum dimension throughout. Renal pelvis is also markedly congested. Renal cortex is approximately 4mm thick. Immuno: CD68 positive,pancytokeratin negative, EMA negative
casos.comentario: This was a straightforward case of xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (XPN) with high agreement (97.3%). Category 2 (malakoplakia) and category 3 (chronic obstructive pyelonephritis) were on a show of hands considered similar (although less preferable terms) and as most people making a diagnosis of malakoplakia had indicated they would perform additional stains (PAS, Von kossa) to look for Michaelis Gutmann bodies it was agreed to merge these with XPN with 100% receiving full marks.

casos.clinica: Right Nephroureterectomy for lower 1/3 ureteric tumour. Specimen: Ureter Tumour. Macro: Ureteric tumour-100mm length and 15mm width, lying 7mm above the distal ureteric resection margin. Immuno: None
casos.comentario: This case was a poorly differentiated ureteric TCC which showed focal lymphoepitheliomatous changes and included a supplementary question regarding stage. It was agreed that categories 1-4 be merged for scoring and awarded full marks. After considerable discussion and following a show of hands it was agreed that categories 5-7 should be awarded half marks, as these variants portend a worse prognosis. Category 8 (squamous cell carcinoma) was regarded incorrect and scored 0. There were numerous comments on the difficulty of assessment of stage due to marked fibro-inflammatory changes at the invasive interface. A number of people had indicated they would have performed pancytokeratin markers (+/- smooth muscle markers) to try and better define the edge of the muscularis propria. It was suggested that stage pT2 (at least) was probably the best descriptor of stage and it was agreed to merge categories 1 & 2 (pT2 & pT3) and as this resulted in 100% of Participants getting the correct answer this supplementary question would be removed for scoring purposes and only the first part of the case scored.

casos.clinica: Hx of TCC bladder G2 and G3. Red patch anterior wall? CIS. Specimen: Bladder biopsies. Macro: Two fragments 6x5x3mm and 5x5x4mm, all taken. Immuno: None
casos.comentario: This was a straightforward case of a nephrogenic adenoma/metaplasia with papillary and tubular/glandular features correctly diagnosed by 96.3% of participants. Categories 2-4 were regarded incorrect and scored 0.

casos.clinica: Right Nephrectomy. Specimen: Kidney Tumour. Macro: 38mm tumour in upper pole of right kidney. The tumour had a yellow and dark haemorrhogic appearance. No evidence of perinephric or renal sinus invasion. Immuno: N/A
casos.comentario: This was a straightforward case of clear cell renal cell carcinoma correctly diagnosed by 94.6% of respondents. All other categories 2-6 were regarded incorrect and scored 0.

casos.clinica: Uterus and bilateral tubes and ovaries removed for endometriosis. No reason given for bladder biopsy. Macro: Small fragments (all embedded). Specimen: Bladder biopsy

Upper pole mass ? RCC. Specimen: Partial nephrectomy. Macro: Within the kidney confined by the capsule was a tan coloured partly haemorrhagic mass measuring 35mm maximally. Immuno: Positive membranous staining with CK7
casos.comentario: This tumour had eosinophilic cytoplasm and well defined cell boundaries. The CK7 immunostain, which was available to review via the website, showed strong diffuse cytoplasmic staining. This was deemed classical for chromophobe carcinoma. Some Participants had made comments on Fuhrman grade but this is not recommended in these tumours.

casos.clinica: 7 cm mass. Right radical nephrectomy. Specimen: Kidney. Macro: Multiloculated cortical cystic lesion with some solid areas measuring 55x87x65 mm. No sinus fat/perinephric fat or vascular invasion seen. Immuno: N/A
casos.diagnostico: mixed epithelial and stromal tumour/ cystic nephromas
casos.comentario: This tumour consisted of cysts with intervening fibrous stroma - with a suggestion of ovarian like stroma. There was pleomorphism in the epithelium lining the cysts but the critical feature to recognise is the stroma. Although these are rare the audience felt that many had made this diagnosis. There is still controversy about whether mixed epithelial and stromal tumour and cystic nephromas where the same entity and as a result these were both scored as correct. One Participant used the other category and stated multicystic nephroma and the audience felt that leeway should be given and they would receive a score of 1. The other diagnoses were considered incorrect.

casos.clinica: New bladder tumour. Clinically invasive. Specimen: Tissue chippings. Macro: 18g of firm and friable tissue chippings. Immuno: N/A
casos.comentario: This was a poorly differentiated tumour and was extremely pleomorphic. The meeting felt that TCC was the most appropriate terminology but there were no convincing neuroendocrine features. There was detrusor muscle invasion present and the supplementary question addressed this. As a result the score was split between these two parts.

casos.clinica: Previous TCC. Also has metastatic melanoma (head and neck). Tumour around bladder neck and "pigmented" tumour left postero - lateral wall. Specimen: Bladder biopsy. Macro: Multiple fragments of brownish tissue aggregated at 25mm. Immuno: Positive: Melan A and S100 Negative: Cam 5.2 and MNF 116
casos.comentario: The immunoprofile of S100 positivity was given in this case which made it straightforward unfortunately it is not possible to give all the possible metastatic tumours in the diagnosis categories as the list would be extremely long. The meeting felt that as a result both submitted responses were correct. (Malignant melanoma 96.1% and Metastatic tumour 3.9%).

casos.clinica: TUR of recurrence of tumour dome. Ureteric bladder tumour. Specimen: Urinary Bladder biopsy. Macro: Three tan fragments the largest 10x5x3mm,the smallest 5x3x2 mm. [3(1); NR]. Immuno: N/A
casos.comentario: Adenocarcinomas in the dome of the bladder are popular cases for the EQA and many Participants commented on the possibility of involvement by colonic tumour or metastasis. The original diagnosis was a signet ring adenocarcinoma but it was felt that adenocarcinoma and its variants were correct as they would probably be treated in a similar fashion. TCC with glandular differentiation was felt to be incorrect. Nephrogenic metaplasia was incorrect. The clinical history was of a recurrent tumour and this would favour a primary bladder tumour - as a result metastatic tumour was felt to be less likely and scored 0.5.

casos.clinica: Bulky bladder mass. Specimen: Bladder. Macro: bladder chippings. Immuno: positive CD56,SYNAPTOPHYSIN and weak staining by chromogranin. CD 45 and MNF 116 are negative. Proliferation index with Ki67 is high
casos.comentario: Neuroendocrine tumours of the bladder are popular cases for the EQA and this case showed crush artefact and necrosis. The Ki67 was also commented on as being high. This would exclude a low grade neuroendocrine tumour (such as carcinoid or paraganglioma). Although metastatic tumours should always be considered this was deemed as incorrect. Small cell and neuroendocrine carcinoma were scored as correct. There were comments that we should use the WHO classification of neuroendocrine tumours should be divided into low (carcinoid), intermediate (atypical carcinoid) and high grade (small & large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma).

casos.clinica: Left upper pole renal mass, sickle cell trait. Specimen: Partial nephrectomy. Macro: Partial nephrectomy of the upper pole measuring 50x35x30 mm. At the superior aspect of the specimen there is a partly cystic and partly solid lesion 30x16x20 mm within 2 mm of the surgical resection margin. Immuno: MNF116+, CK7+, vimentin+, CD68-, CD10-, CEA-
casos.comentario: The critical part of this history was the young age (35) and sickle cell trait. Sickle cells were seen in some areas. Renal medullary carcinoma was the preferred diagnosis. Some consider this as a variant of collecting duct carcinoma and this was deemed as scoring 0.5. The other diagnoses were deemed incorrect. Once again the same Participant used other and then added the diagnosis and the meeting was generous in giving this a score of 1 as well.

casos.clinica: Bladder Biopsy. Haematuria. Red Patches. Bladder Biopsies. Macro: 5 tissue fragments.
Previous CIS bladder. Now new lesions. ?Nature
casos.comentario: This slide shows multiple small pieces of bladder mucosa which contain tubular and papillary elements lined by a single layer of bland, low cuboidal epithelium. This is nephrogenic metaplasia.

casos.clinica: Haematuria. Bladder biopsy.
Lesion in left kidney
casos.comentario: This slightly blurry slide shows features of a conventional renal cell carcinoma.

casos.clinica: History of G3 pT1 TCC Bladder. Stopped BCG after 12 instillations. Cystoscopy showed velvety area posterior bladder wall. Cold cup biopsy from velvety area ? Recurrent TCC ? Inflammed. Macro: Two biopsies, together 5 x 3 x 3mm. Specimen: Urinary bladder biopsy.
Haematuria. Irregular trigonal area. Specimen: Urinary bladder biopsy. Macro: Two fragments of tissue measuring 4mm in maximum dimension each. Immuno: None.
casos.comentario: This case had a combination of dilated glands with an inflamed stroma. Cystitis cystica and cystitis glandularis were deemed to be correct. There was mild stromal oedema but not the typical features of polypoidal cystitis and as a result this did not score. The other diagnoses were deemed incorrect.

casos.clinica: Abnormal refills identified on flexible cystoscopy. Specimen: Urinary bladder biopsy. Macro: Two fragments of tissue measuring 3 and 4mm. Immuno: None.
casos.comentario: This was a straightforward case of Schistosomiasis - though one participant commented that there were more organisms on the scanned slide then on the glass slide that they had. Encrusted cystitis was deemed incorrect.

casos.clinica: Haematuria; CTU showed bladder diverticulum confirmed on cystoscopy. Specimen: TURBT. Macro: Several tan coloured fragments, measuring in aggregate 25 mm across. Immuno: None.
casos.comentario: This tumour had definite squamous differentiation and this is clinically significant as often these don't respond to chemotherapy as well as pure TCC. As a result SCC and TCC with squamous differentiation were deemed to be correct, but the other answers were considered as incorrect. Following comments regarding the use of TCC rather than urothelial we have now added the term urothelial to the diagnoses. One participant wanted to use immunohistochemistry to define whether pure SCC vs TCC with squamous differentiation but there is no reliable panel to do this.

casos.clinica: Bladder tumour. Specimen: TURBT. Macro: Grey brown fragments weighing 6 gram. Immuno: CEA +ve, CK7 +ve, CDX2 positive, CK20 +ve, CD15 positive and thrombomodulin negative.
casos.comentario: This case was of an adenocarcinoma in the bladder and as for case P12 there is always a possibility that this was from a colonic primary and although beta catenin expression has been used to differentiate these it really requires radiology and staging. As a result adenocarcinoma (and all it's variants) and metastatic tumour were deemed correct but there was no TCC component and this was considered as incorrect.

casos.clinica: Right upper pole tumour. Specimen: Right radical laproscopic nephrectomy. Macro: 82mm sized upper pole solid brown lesion. No scarring seen. No involvement of renal vein or extension into capsular fat or sinus fat. Immuno: Tumour shows diffuse CK7 positivity, CD10 is negative.
casos.comentario: This was a beautiful example of Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma with prominent cell membranes and a supporting immunoprofile. Agreement was high on this case and all other answers were considered as incorrect. Chromophobe carcinomas should not be Fuhrman graded.

casos.clinica: History of high grade bladder cancer ? Recurrence. Specimen: TURBT. Macro: Multiple fragments 2 gm. Immuno: None.
casos.comentario: Not scored. This was an excellent example of micropapillary TCC, which was submitted as just TCC. This variant is becoming better recognised but only 18% put this answer. This is a high grade tumour that has propensity for vascular invasion, though retraction artefact can mimic this. This entity should be recognised as there is evidence that aggressive treatment is warranted even when only pT1. There was insufficient agreement on the main diagnosis to score this part of the question but the supplementary question asked whether there was vascular invasion and this reach over 70% and the meeting felt that this part could be scored. Indefinite was felt to be incorrect given that 91% put Yes.

casos.clinica: Left open radical nephrectomy + hilar nodes. Appendicectomy. Had pelvic collection. Specimen: Left open radical nephrectomy for renal mass. Macro: Left kidney: A kidney measuring 20cm superior to inferior x15cm medial to lateral x 14cm anterior to posterior. There is a segment of ureter measuring 6x0.5cm. There is tumour measuring 15x11x9cm, involving most of the kidney, which appears to be confined to the kidney. Large areas are necrotic. There is no macroscopic involvement of the renal vein. Immuno: tumour is diffusely positive for WT1, CD57 and PAX8 with scattered focal positivityfor CD56 (NCAM). EMA shows only extremely scanty focal positivity at one edge of the lesion but is negative elsewhere. CK7, racemase (AMACR), TTF-1 and CAIX are negative.
casos.comentario: This case was a metanephric adenoma correctly recognised by over 99% of people. A reference to a recent review article on metanephric adenoma was provided. Interestingly, no one suggested the solid variant of papillary RCC which it was emphasised is the main histological differential. Several people had commented on the immuno overlap with carcinoid tumour but the morphology was not considered typical of a neuroendocrine tumour particularly the nuclear cytomorphology. It was unanimously agreed to regard categories 2, 3 & 4 incorrect.

casos.clinica: Specimen: Bladder biopsy. Macro: Tissue 6mm maximum. Immuno: None performed.
casos.comentario: This case generated considerable discussion. The favoured diagnosis was eosinophilic cystitis but there was also a surface papillary component. Several people commented that papillary cystitis (the reporting Pathologist's diagnosis) was not in the dropdown list but it was emphasised that papillary and polypoid cystsitis are probably best regarded ends of a spectrum (the dropdown to be amended to papillary/polyposis cystitis). Some people had commented on possible catheter reaction and additional clinical information was obtained showing that there was a catheter in situ at the time of biopsy. This information was not provided in the original clinical history however, it was felt this was not critical in recognising the lesion as benign/inflammatory rather than TCC. The consensus was to merge all non-neoplastic responses as correct and categories 3, 4 & 6 as incorrect as this was likely to lead to inappropriate patient management.

casos.clinica: Large 2cm polyp bladder neck, narrow stalk ?benign inverted papilloma. Specimen: Bladder neck tumour. Macro: Pieces of firm tan tissue, together 28x20x8mms. Immuno: None.
casos.comentario: This was a straightforward inverted urothelial papilloma (IP). The regularity of the trabeculae, central streaming and bland cytology were all typical of IP. Several people had commented on the presence of an exophytic component, it was emphasised that the presence of occasional non-branching papillae did not preclude the diagnosis of IP and categories 2-4 were all regarded as incorrect.

casos.clinica: Oncocytoma-right-sided upper pole lesion. Specimen: Right Partial Nephrectomy. Macro: Brown nodular tumour 26x26x30 mm. Immuno: N/A.
casos.comentario: This was a controversial case and had generated a large number of comments from Participants. Although the case reached the threshold consensus for scoring there were a number of reasons the meeting decided to exclude the case from scoring. A very high number of people (>100) had requested immuno (although interestingly this had not been performed by the reporting Pathologist). A number of people had commented on the presence of necrosis (which would be a concerning feature when making an oncocytoma diagnosis) and raised the possibility of either pre-operative biopsy or embolization. Additional clinical history was ascertained from the reporting Pathologist and there had been a biopsy prior to the resection specimen, which also explained the fibrosis and microtubular reaction at the edge of the biopsy site.

casos.clinica: Solid lesion left side ?TCC ?adenoCa. Specimen: Bladder tumour. Macro: 8g of bladder tissue. All embedded. Immuno: None performed.
casos.comentario: This was a straightforward case of endometriosis of the bladder. As in previous circulations categories 1 & 2 were merged (It was highlighted that focally some of the glandular epithelium was ciliated and that Mullerianosis might be the most precise terminology). Neither of the Participants offering cystitis glandularis or adenocarcinoma had mentioned endometriosis on the response form and were marked 0.

casos.clinica: Kidney tumour, partial nephrectomy. Specimen: H&E is of tumour and adjacent uninvolved kidney. Macro: 3cm well circumscribed tumour with tan, variegated cut surface. Immuno: Pan-cytokeratin (AE1/3) focally positive, Vimentin positive, CD10 focally positive, HMB45 negative, TFE3 (done elsewhere) positive. FISH analysis (done elsewhere): TFE3 gene rearrangement.
casos.comentario: This was a case of TFE-3 translocation renal cell carcinoma, for which the results of TFE3 immuno staining and TFE 3 +ve FISH were provided, leading a small number of people to comment that the case was unsuitable for EQA, given that you 'didn't really need to look at the slide'. However, there was not 100% agreement for the correct answer. There were a small number of comments pointing out this was an Xp11 & not a t(6;11) translocation renal cell carcinoma. The terminology in the dropdown box had tried to incorporate the recent proposed nomenclature from the ISUP Vancouver classification on RCC and been inclusive of both translocation types and will be slightly reworded as Renal cell carcinoma - MiT Family Translocation RCC (including Xp11 & t[6;11]) to avoid future confusion. Category 7 was merged with 1 as the terminology in the dropdown may have explained the use of the other category (although again it was pointed out not to use this when the response was already provided in the dropdown menu). The meeting strongly favoured on a show of hands that all the remaining categories should all get 0.

casos.clinica: Previous history of a G2 pTa urothelial carcinoma and previous carcinoma in situ both of which had been refractory to BCG therapy. Specimen: Cystectomy. Macro: None specified. Immuno: N/A.
casos.comentario: This was a straightforward case of urothelial carcinoma in situ of the bladder from a cystectomy specimen, which we were told in the clinical history had been performed for BCG failure and showed focally prominent pagetoid extension. A relatively small number of people requested immuno to rule out other possible differentials e.g. melanoma and extramammary Paget's (the latter being extremely uncommon in the bladder). The meeting felt that especially given the history, this was a morphological diagnosis and awarded category 1 full marks and all the other responses 0. There were quite a large number of comments about the use of TCC rather than urothelial carcinoma in the dropdown box, urothelial carcinoma being the preferred term in the WHO classification. It was therefore decided to edit these categories in the dropdown menu to TCC/urothelial carcinoma.

casos.clinica: Superficial tumour. Specimen: TUR Bladder tumour. Macro: About 0.5 grams of tissue fragments. Immuno: None.
casos.comentario: This was a straightforward case of papillary TCC / urothelial carcinoma. The vast majority favoured that it was a low grade lesion in the new (WHO 2004) terminology and grade 2 in the old (WHO 1973). On a show of hands TCC in situ (which by definition is a flat lesion) and TCC plasmacytoid (which is a variant of invasive TCC /urothelial carcinoma) were regarded incorrect and awarded 0. For the supplementary question the was very high agreement (96%) that this was non-invasive (pTa). pT1 was regarded incorrect and awarded 0 as was pTis which the meeting felt was incorrect given this was clearly a papillary lesion.

casos.clinica: Bladder tumour ? invasive TCC. Specimen: TURBT. Macro: 28g of friable tissue chippings. Immuno: CK20, CEA and CDX2 positive. CK7, PSA and TTF1 negative.
casos.comentario: This was a case of adenocarcinoma with an enteric pattern involving the bladder. It was emphasised that because of immuno overlap, clinical & radiological correlation are required to separate a bladder primary from secondary involvement from a colorectal primary. The submitting Pathologist disclosed in their diagnosis that a sigmoid tumour was subsequently confirmed clinically. As this was not known to Participants it was the meeting consensus to score all adenocarcinoma answers as correct and metastatic tumour (as people proving this response had mentioned colorectal adenocarcinoma in their comments). Villous adenoma (a benign entity) and TCC with glandular differentiation were regarded incorrect and marked 0 as the clinical implications for both these diagnoses were potentially significant.

casos.clinica: Persistent hematuria. Cystoscopy showed a solid-looking bladder tumour. TURBT performed. Section from the bladder chippings. Immuno: None.
casos.diagnostico: Carcinoma (Urothelial Ca with squamous differentiation / squamous cell Ca) +/- schistosomiasis
casos.comentario: Original diagnosis: squamous cell Ca with schistosomiasis. Most participants did not mention schistosomiasis. There was debate about whether the organisms could be seen in all sections and whether it was possible to say this case represented pure squamous cell Ca or transitional cell Ca with squamous differentiation.

casos.clinica: Lap R radical nephrectomy. Specimen: Nephrectomy with well-defined unencapsulated mahogany brown tumour with a central scar in the upper pole. Immuno: CK7 positive (patchy).
casos.comentario: Original diagnosis: oncocytoma

casos.clinica: Rt radical orchidectomy. Normal tumour markers. Previous Lt orchidectomy for undescended testis. Specimen: 8mm solid grey nodule within testis. Immuno: OCT3/4, CD30 and AFP negative.
casos.comentario:
Original diagnosis: spermatocytic seminoma. No consensus reached with a similar number of participants putting classical seminoma as spermatocytic seminoma.
This was felt to be an example of spermatocytic seminoma (OCT3/4 negative, three cell type morphology, lack of infiltrating lymphocytes). Differentiation from classical seminoma is important because these tumours require only orchidectomy; they do not metastasise and adjuvant therapy is not indicated. They show intratubular spread/growth but ITGCN is not a feature.

casos.clinica: Para-aortic mass biopsy. 4 pieces of tissue, the largest 18mm in maximum dimension. Testes are clinically normal. Immuno: PLAP strongly positive, CD117 positive, patchy positivity for CD30 and HCG. Background lymphocytes positive for CD45, CD3, CD5 and CD20. ALK1, CK8/18, AE1/3 negative.
casos.comentario:
Original diagnosis: seminoma. Diagnoses of seminoma and mixed germ cell tumour (including references to an embryonal carcinoma
component) were considered acceptable responses as these would be treated similarly. Answers referring to choriocarcinoma were deemed unacceptable as this diagnosis carries implications for treatment.

CD79a equivocal. Ki-67 25%. Scattered S100 positive cells. CD20, CD3, CD5, Bob-1, ALK1, CD138, CD34, Cyclin D1, CK8/18, CKAE1/3, CD68, CD15 all negative.
