casos.clinica: Multifocal papillary lesions in the bladder. History of superficial bladder tumours. ?Recurrence. Specimen: Bladder biopsy.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case caused considerable debate. The most popular diagnosis was nephrogenic adenoma/metaplasia made by 88% of respondents. It was agreed that categories 1, 2, 5 and 10 should be merged for scoring purposes, although there was some disagreement as to some of the secondary diagnoses that went with this diagnosis in categories 2 and 5. Clear cell adenocarcinoma was considered wrong. Categories 3, 6, 8 and 9 were felt to represent benign/proliferative lesions and on a show of hands, people voted that these responses merited half, rather than full marks.

casos.clinica: Previous TCC. Specimen: Bladder biopsy. Macro: None given.
casos.diagnostico: Transitional cell carcinoma, G3 pT1 and ?pT2+CIS
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case produced a wide range of responses and provoked considerable debate. The meeting unanimously felt this was invasive urothelial carcinoma. pT1 was marginally favored in the responses over pT2 disease by those who specified stage. A small number of people called this non-invasive (pTa). The difficulty of entering multiple responses into the OMNIS database was highlighted. The meeting felt that any response indicating invasive disease should be merged for scoring purposes. Unfortunately, in several categories (4 & 8) TCC not otherwise specified had been merged, at the data entry stage, with TCC invasive (no specific stage provided) and therefore it has not been possible to score the case in the manner proposed at the meeting and the Organiser has therefore excluded the case for scoring purposes. It was agreed that in future cases of TCC, the submitting pathologist should indicate the feature required from the participant i.e. grade or stage. Failure to provide this in the Participants response will result in 0 marks. A recent paper highlighting the difficulties in small biopsies discriminating hyperplastic muscularis mucosae from muscularis propria was presented. Furthermore the reporting pathologist had clearly found the discrimination between pT1 and pT2 difficult in this case, which clearly had significant educational value. BAUP intends to address bladder tumour staging in a forthcoming workshop.

casos.clinica: Cystic tumour upper pole of right kidney - partial nephrectomy. Tumour ruptured. Total nephrectomy. No immunohistochemistry performed. Specimen: Kidney. Macro: Upper pole of kidney, 60 x 60 x 30mm largely replaced by tumour which is disrupted making overall measurement difficult. Tumour appears confined by renal capsule.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
The overwhelming consensus was that this was papillary renal cell carcinoma and that for scoring purposes diagnostic categories 1�4 and 6 should be merged. Papillary variant of clear cell carcinoma was felt to be a specific entity that might wrongly infer a translocation carcinoma and should therefore be awarded half marks. The roughly equal split between pathologists diagnosing Eble type I and type II in this case was emphasized.

casos.clinica: ?Tumour. Specimen: Bladder biopsy. Macro: A single fragment of tissue, 4mm in maximum dimension.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
There was strong agreement this biopsy represented inverted papilloma (91%). Several images were show to emphasize the differing amounts of tissue in some of the sections. The meeting felt that inverted and papillary TCC was incorrect. It was commented on that inverted papilloma is followed up clinically in the same way as superficial TCC in many institutions. Cystitis cystica and hyperplastic von Brunn's nests were felt not to be specific enough and should be awarded half marks.

casos.clinica: Specimen: Kidney. Macro: Tan coloured tumour (143 x 120 x 100mm) upper pole left kidney.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a case of renal oncocytoma correctly diagnosed by over 90% of respondents. The meeting felt that this was a morphological diagnosis which could be made on the section provided without additional studies such as immunohistochemistry or electron microscopy. Categories 2�5 and 7 were regarded as wrong. Diagnostic category 6 (oncocytic tumour) was not felt to be a specific diagnosis and on a show of hands it was agreed to award this response half marks.

casos.clinica: Pedunculated bladder tumour with 1 sm satellite. Foot of tumour seemed v. firm. ?Invasive. Not completely resected. Immuno's - Epithelial elements - positive for pan-cytokeratin, CK5/6, CK19, CK20, 34BE12, CAM 5.2. Giant cell and mononuclear elements - negative with above epithelial markers, do not express BHCG. Strongly positive with Vimentin, CD68 and tartrate resistant acid phos. Specimen: Bladder bx.
casos.diagnostico: Papillary urothelial carcinoma combined with giant cell tumour
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was an educational case of papillary transitional cell carcinoma combined with an unusual giant cell tumour (osteoclast-like giant cell) reaction. The submitting Pathologist kindly submitted some images of the immunohistochemistry, which helped highlight a minor invasive component, which may not have been present in all the circulated sections. The important differentials namely, the giant cell variant of transitional cell carcinoma and TCC with syncytiotrophoblastic differentiation were highlighted.

casos.clinica: Haematuria. Specimen: Bladder Biopsy.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a straightforward case of schistosomiasis with viable eggs, eliciting a florid eosinophilic cystitis. It was agreed to merge schistosomiasis and eosinophilic cystitis with schistosomiasis for scoring purposes, meaning all respondents were awarded full marks.

casos.clinica: Large renal mass noted as multicystic on U/S. Nephrectomy: Kidney with 160mm diameter well circumscribed multicystic tumour. Representative slide. Specimen: Kidney.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case resulted in a range of terminologies for similar diagnostic entities. Categories 1, 2, 4 & 6 being differing terms for cystic nephroma and 3, 5 and 8 equivalent to mixed epithelial stromal tumour (MEST). The summary of a recent paper from Am J Surg Path, which proposed that cystic nephroma and MEST are similar enough to justify re-classification as renal epithelial stromal tumours (REST) was presented. For scoring purposes it was therefore unanimously agreed to merge categories 1�6 and 8. Multicystic renal cell carcinoma, tubular cystic carcinoma (low grade collecting duct carcinoma) and the entities in category 10 (other) were deemed incorrect for scoring.

casos.clinica: Cystoprostatectomy for bladder tumour
casos.comentario:
This is a section of bladder showing a grade 3 (high grade) urothelial carcinoma which is seen to invade the lamina propria and, superficially, the detrusor muscle.
Much of the background surface epithelium is denuded but urothelium (including carcinoma-in-situ) is seen in prominent von Brunn's nests.

casos.clinica: Symptoms not known. Fronded tumour on trigone at TURBT. Specimen: Bladder biopsy. Macro: 1ml polypoid tissue - not embedded.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
There was very high agreement that this case represented inverted papilloma (96% of responses). Several participants commented on the presence of occasional papillae and the clinical description as 'fronded', but the meeting felt there was less architectural and cytological atypia than would be expected for either PUNLMP or inverted TCC. Responses 2 and 4 were therefore regarded as incorrect. Inverted papilloma with atypia was agreed to merit half marks.

casos.clinica: 11cm diameter tumour in right kidney. Specimen: H&E and Photo of CK7
casos.diagnostico: Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma G2, pT2
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a case of chromophobe renal cell carcinoma. It was pointed out that in the WHO 2004 classification the eosinophilic variant is reserved for cases showing purely eosinophilic cells with prominent cell membranes. A small number of participants commented that the CK7 photo was not included with the circulated slides. The meeting felt the diagnosis was tenable on morphological grounds and therefore categories 2�5 should be regarded as incorrect for scoring.

casos.clinica:
Right renal mass. Specimen: Right nephrectomy.
Macro: 85mm diameter uniform pale brown tumour confined to the kidney.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a case of renal oncocytoma correctly identified by >90% of respondents. Diagnostic categories 2�5 were regarded as incorrect by the meeting. The comments made by 2 participants in their responses that this case was unsuitable for EQA on the grounds of lack of information and that it should be excluded from scoring was highlighted. There was a strong consensus at the meeting refuting these comments and it was unanimously agreed the case was suitable for scoring.

casos.clinica:
Mass left kidney. Specimen: Partial nephrectomy.
Macro: Partial nephrectomy 50 x 35 x 32mm containing a firm yellow tumour 32mm maximum.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
The consensus opinion was that this case represented papillary renal cell carcinoma. It was agreed to merge categories 1, 3, 4, 5 and 7 as papillary RCC for scoring purposes. Metanephric adenoma, tubopapillary adenoma and renocortical adenoma (2, 6 and 8) were all regarded as incorrect. The meeting felt the diagnosis of papillary renal cell carcinoma was tenable without immunohistochemistry which, it was pointed out, was actually performed by the reporting Pathologist, but was not submitted with the clinical information for the case.

casos.clinica:
Pyrexia, rigors, anaemia. Renal mass with lung lesions on CT. Immuno: CK7 negative. EMA positive. Vimentin positive. LeuM1 (CD15) negative.
CD10 +/- Specimen: Kidney. Macro: Duplex ureter with soft white mass 45mm and polypoid extension into lower calyceal system.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case provoked considerable discussion and was excluded for scoring purposes on the grounds of lack of a consensus diagnosis. The favored diagnosis and that of the reporting pathologist was collecting duct carcinoma. The overlap between this and renal medullary carcinoma was briefly discussed together with some of the other proffered diagnoses.

casos.clinica:
New diagnosis bladder tumour. Specimen: Bladder.
Macro: 32g tissue chippings.
casos.diagnostico: Transitional cell carcinoma of bladder, G3 pT2
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case was also excluded for scoring purposes due to lack of a consensus diagnosis. There was a spectrum of diagnoses from urothelial carcinoma with various forms of divergent differentiation to a poorly differentiated malignant tumour requiring immuno for diagnosis. Immunohistochemistry was not to our knowledge performed on the original case which was reported as transitional cell carcinoma, G3, pT2.

casos.clinica: Specimen: Bladder biopsy. Macro: 0.9g of tissue fragments. All processed.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
Most participants recognised this as adenocarcinoma with signet ring and mucinous features and indicated this could either represent primary bladder origin or a metastasis or direct spread from another site and that this distinction required clinical and radiological correlation. The meeting agreed that for scoring purposes, any response with adenocarcinoma +/- mucinous or signet ring should be merged for scoring purposes. Categories 4 and 6 (lipid rich urothelial carcinoma and TCC with glandular differentiation) were regarded as incorrect.

casos.clinica:
Multiple bulbous areas in bladder with erythema.
Specimen: Bladder biopsy. Macro: None given.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a case of endometriosis, correctly identified by more than 98% of respondents. Diagnostic categories 2, 3 and 4 (cystitis cystica, endometriosis-like adenofibromas and endocervicosis) were regarded as incorrect for scoring by the meeting.

casos.clinica:
FOR EDUCATION/INTEREST ONLY. Clinical left RCC. Immuno: WT1 and CD57 positive. CK7 and CD15 negative. Specimen: Left kidney.
Macro: Kidney with circumscribed mass measuring 58mm in lower pole. Cut surface showed a cream tan colour.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case was also for education/interest only and represented a metanephric adenoma. A summary slide emphasizing the immunohistochemical difference between this and papillary renal cell carcinoma, which is the main histological differential, was shown.

casos.clinica: Ca rectum 1985 - DXT and anterior resection 1985. Large bladder tumour on right wall/dome ?TCC. ?Recurrence. Incomplete resection. Immuno: CD56 +, TTF1 +, CK7 -, CK20 -, EMA. Specimen: Bladder tissue. Macro: Fragments of bladder tissue.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
The consensus agreement was this case was small cell carcinoma with an additional sarcomatoid carcinoma component. It was agreed to disregard stage for scoring purposes as significant numbers of Pathologists had not included a stage (as requested) and to merge categories 1, 3 and 5. The meeting agreed that the presence of a sarcomatoid component argued towards primary bladder origin and it was emphasized that extrapulmonary small cell carcinoma can be TTF-1 positive, as in this case. It was therefore decided to award categories 2, 4 and 7 which favored metastatic small cell half marks and category 6 (carcinosarcoma) was regarded as incorrect, due to a failure to specifically mention small cell carcinoma which could have had therapeutic implications.

casos.clinica:
Tumour upper pole right kidney. Nephrectomy performed. Specimen: Nephrectomy specimen.
Macro: On gross examination the kidney showed a circumscribed soft brownish nodule measuring 35 x 33mm situated in the outer cortex and bulging into the perinephric fat.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case was excluded for scoring purposes on the basis of the lack of a consensus diagnosis and generated a wide range of benign and malignant diagnoses. Large numbers of Participants commented on the need for immunohistochemistry, which was performed at the time of diagnosis but was not provided by the submitting Pathologist. The importance of providing all the information available to the reporting Pathologist at the time of diagnosis, when submitting a case, was emphasized. The diagnosis in this case was actually changed from xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis to angiomyolipoma following additional immunohistochemistry (HMB-45 & melan A both +ve), performed after contacting the submitting Pathologist. An amended report has subsequently been issued to the relevant Clinicians.

casos.clinica: Long-standing chronic urinary symptoms. Found to have bladder tumour. Given neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by cystectomy. Specimen: Cystectomy specimen. Macro: None given.
casos.diagnostico: Poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of bladder, pT2a,N0
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case generated considerable discussion. It was the consensus of the meeting that a correct answer required identification of both a carcinoma component and schistosomiasis. Because of the relatively limited amount of tumour and lack of a background in-situ component, it was agreed that either TCC and/or squamous cell carcinoma was acceptable and therefore categories 1, 2, 3 and 4 should be merged for scoring. Categories 4 and 7 failed to mention schistosomiasis and were therefore awarded half marks. Category 6 which only mentioned schistosomiasis and failed to mention malignancy was felt on a show of hands to merit no marks.

casos.clinica: Laparoscopic left nephrectomy for tumour. Immuno: CK7 (+), EMA membranous positivity, CD10 (-), AE1/AE3 (+), PAS (+). Specimen: Partial left nephrectomy. Macro: Partial nephrectomy 30 x 30 x 40mm. Cut surface shows a well circumscribed tumour measuring 25 x 25 x 25mm. Cut surface is greyish white. Does not breach capsule. Clear of margins.
casos.diagnostico: Mucinous tubular and spindle cell carcinoma, pT1
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
There was strong agreement that this was a mucinous tubular and spindle cell carcinoma which was the most popular response by 72% of Participants. As this failed to reach the specified 80% level of agreement required for a scoring case, it was excluded. However, a number of people felt that this was a 'good EQA case', despite the written comments on a small number of response forms that it was too rare an entity for a scoring case. Interestingly, on a show of hands a substantial proportion of the audience present had made this diagnosis in routine practice.

casos.clinica: Tumour at bladder neck. ?Some normal prostate removed as well. Specimen: Bladder chips. Macro: 5.6g of tissue chips. All processed in 4 blocks. Sections from representative block circulated.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case provoked considerable discussion. There was strong agreement the diagnosis was inverted papilloma (IP) (95% agreement). However, it was pointed out at the meeting that diagnostic criteria for IP vary and because there was at least a focal exophytic (papillary) component in this case, that inverted growth pattern TCC should be merged with IP for scoring purposes. Category 3 was regarded as incorrect.

casos.clinica: Left renal tumour, some nodes on CT sent en bloc. Specimen: Renal tumour. Macro: Two tumours present, the larger maximum diameter 57mm, the smaller maximum diameter 22mm and extending into perinephric fat. Both tumours have brownish cut surfaces, with no obvious scars. Section from smaller lesion.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
There was strong agreement this case represented a small renal oncocytoma showing cellular infiltration of fat. It was emphasized this feature is acceptable for oncocytoma, although this had obviously caused some diagnostic difficulty/uncertainty for some Participants and caused them to favor a diagnosis of chromophobe RCC. The meeting felt this was a 'good EQA case', but because it marginally failed with 75% agreement to reach the 80% threshold, that it had to be excluded for scoring purposes.

casos.clinica: FOR EDUCATION AND INTEREST ONLY. Presented with pyrexia, cough, night sweats. Scans showed right renal mass and multiple pulmonary metastases. Immuno: Positive for CK7, CK5/6 and 34BE12. Negative for CK20, TTF1 and Calretinin. Specimen: Right nephrectomy. Macro: 10.5 x 8 x 7.5cm haemorrhagic and yellow tumour in right kidney.
casos.diagnostico: Collecting duct carcinoma, Fuhrman grade IV
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case was submitted for education and interest only and was not presented formally at the meeting due to time constraints. The favored diagnosis from the submitted responses was collecting duct carcinoma which was also the submitting Pathologist's diagnosis and was supported by the expression of high molecular weight cytokeratins. A considerable range of other tumour types were proffered by Participants.

casos.clinica: FOR EDUCATION AND INTEREST ONLY. Tetraplegia. On urinary catheter for 30 years. Presented with haematuria and a solid bladder tumour. TURBT performed. Specimen: Bladder. Macro: None given
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was also an educational case with the main differential from the submitted responses between adenocarcinoma and nephrogenic adenoma/metaplasia. The case had actually been referred to a specialist Uropathologist in America for second opinion who also found the case diagnostically challenging and favored the diagnosis of urothelial carcinoma with glandular differentiation, rather than pure adenocarcinoma. The presence of detrusor muscle invasion and focally quite marked cytological atypia were argued as features that supported a malignant over a benign (particularly nephrogenic adenoma/metaplasia) diagnosis.

casos.clinica: Haematuria. No TURBT no mass post resection. Immuno: CK7 and bcl2 strongly positive in tumour cells CK20 and CDX 2 focally positive in tumour cells, vimentin, CA 125 and ER negative. Specimen: Bladder tumour Macro: Pieces of pale tan tissue weighing 1gm.
casos.diagnostico: Carcinoma favouring primary adenocarcinoma of bladder
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a contentious case. The favored diagnosis by the Participants was adenocarcinoma with differing interpretation as to whether this represented a bladder or non-bladder primary. In addition to a malignant glandular component there was also a solid poorly differentiated area in the biopsy which resulted in a significant number of Participants favoring a diagnosis of TCC with glandular differentiation rather than pure adenocarcinoma. Due to lack of consensus agreement this case was excluded for scoring purposes. It was emphasized that the overlap in immunohistochemistry between primary and non-bladder primary adenocarcinoma was significant and that this distinction required both clinical and radiological correlation.

casos.clinica:
Complex cyst lower pole of left kidney. ?Malignant ?margins. Specimen:
Partial nephrectomy. Macro: The specimen consists of the lower pole of kidney measuring 60x45x35mm, bearing a mass measuring 50x25x35mm. On cut section, two lesions are grossly identified - 1 superficial & soft haemorrhagic mass measuring 50x 35x30mm & a further deeper & solid partly necrotic mass, measuring 35x20x25mm. Both surfaces inked green. Grossly, the renal resection margin is at least 5mm away from the deep necrotic mass as described.
casos.diagnostico: Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma, Stage pT2, Nx, Mx
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
There was strong agreement (96%) this case represented chromophobe renal cell carcinoma with classical cytomorphology. A number of participants had commented on not receiving the immuno and PAS photos and the point was made that in future circulations with photos included, these would also be posted on the EQA website. The meeting felt that although further immuno, Hale's colloidal iron and electron microscopy had been suggested by some people, that the diagnosis was achievable on the basis of the H&E morphology. Categories 2, 3 and 4 were therefore regarded as incorrect for scoring purposes.

casos.clinica: Tumour at dome. Immuno: Cytokeratin 20+ve cytokeratin 7 -ve. Specimen: Bladder (cystectomy). Macro: 70 x 65 x 25mm tumour in dome of bladder.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a case of mucinous/signet ring adenocarcinoma. A high proportion of Participants suggested possible primary urachal origin, given the specified location in the dome, but a significant number of Participants favored a non-bladder primary on the basis of the immuno profile (CK 20+ve & CK 7 -ve). Most people stressed the need for clinical/radiological/pathological correlation in establishing the primary site. For scoring purposes it was agreed to merge all adenocarcinoma diagnoses 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and that glandular metaplasia with extravasated mucin was incorrect.

casos.clinica: No clinical information provided. Specimen: Not stated. Macro: Renal tumour 14 x 10 x 5.5cm.
casos.diagnostico: Conventional renal cell carcinoma with sarcomatoid areas. Fuhrman grade 4
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case caused considerable debate and was complicated by the presence of multiple diagnostic features in the same section. There was strong agreement this represented conventional/clear cell renal cell carcinoma with sarcomatoid differentiation, but the meeting could not agree on how to score the remaining diagnostic categories 2, 3 and 4 and therefore the case was excluded for scoring purposes. This section also showed vascular invasion, coagulative necrosis and focal rhabdoid differentiation.

casos.clinica: FOR EDUCATION AND INTEREST ONLY. Horse shoe kidney containing anterior tumour with metastatic regional lymph nodes. Specimen: Horse shoe kidney. Macro: On gross examination the kidney showed a 60 x 50 mm soft yellowish brown variegated tumour with focal haemorrhage infiltrating the perinephric and sinus fat. The retro-caval and para-caval lymph nodes contained metastasis.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case was for education and interest only and was not presented formally at the meeting. The case was a renal carcinoid which was also the favoured diagnosis of the Participants. It should be emphasized that primary renal carcinoid has a know association with horseshoe kidney.

casos.clinica: FOR EDUCATION AND INTEREST ONLY. History of haematuria. Cystoscopy - suspicious area inside bladder neck - ?ca bladder ?ca prostate. Immuno: CK20 CK7 positive. PSA and PSAP negative. Specimen: Bladder biopsies. Macro: None given.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case was for education and interest only and was not presented formally at the meeting. It was submitted as a case of infiltrative transitional cell carcinoma. The invasive component showed a range of divergent differentiation including lipoid cell, clear cell, nested and micro-cystic areas. There was also background carcinoma in situ.

casos.clinica: Upper urinary tract obstruction. Nodule seen on cytoscopy. Previous history of breast carcinoma. Immunohistochemistry: CK7 positive, ER positive. Specimen: Bladder biopsy. Macro: Two greyish tissue pieces aggregating 7mm.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
There was high agreement (98%) that this case represented metastatic breast carcinoma and the majority of participants suggested this was of lobular type. The meeting consensus was that on the basis of the clinical history and the immunoprofile (CK7 and ER positive) provided that metastatic adenocarcinoma without specifying breast merited half marks and the remaining categories 3, 4, 5 & 6 should be regarded as incorrect for scoring purposes.

casos.clinica:
Left RCC. Immuno: CK7, EMA, Vimentin, AMACR- Positive. 34BE12- Focal Positive. E-Cadherin - Negative. Specimen: Nephrectomy for tumour.
Macro: Tumour at upper pole 86x80x65mm with a variegated yellow and haemorrhagic appearence on cut surface.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a case of papillary renal cell carcinoma and Eble type 1 was the favoured subtype. The meeting consensus was that categories 1, 2 and 6 should be merged for scoring purposes, giving a high level of agreement (94%). Categories 5 and 7 (papillary and clear cell & RC mixed papillary and solid ? translocation associated, respectively) were felt to merit half marks for at least partial recognition of a papillary component, the other categories 3, 4 and 8 were regarded as incorrect for scoring purposes.

casos.clinica: Left renal RCC, left Kidney. Specimen: Left kidney. Macro: Kidney measuring 9.8x5.5x4.0cm with a brown tumour 3.2cm diameter in the midzone. Tumour is dark brown with an area of scarring/calcification.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a straight forward case of renal oncocytoma with a high level of agreement (98%). A small number of participants had proffered a diagnosis of eosinophilic renal cell tumour requiring immuno, but the consensus of the meeting was that oncocytoma was diagnosable on morphological grounds and it was noted that immuno had not been performed at the reporting institution, as the morphological features were also regarded as 'sufficient for diagnosis'. Accordingly, categories 2, 3 and 4 (chromophobe RCC, oncocytic renal cell carcinoma and eosinophilic renal cell tumour needs immuno +/-EM, respectively) were regarded as incorrect for scoring.

casos.clinica: Extensive bladder tumour? Extending into prostate. Immuno: CK5 positive. Specimen: TURBT. Macro: 11grams of bladder chippings.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case requested morphological diagnosis and stage. In relation to the former, SCC was favoured over transitional cell carcinoma with squamous differentiation. It was highlighted that 31 participants had commented on the presence of concomitant urothelial carcinoma in situ and therefore according to the WHO 2004 classification, TCC with squamous differentiation was the most appropriate terminology. It was decided to score the case on the basis of stage for which there was high agreement this was pT2 (at least), therefore categories 1, 2 and 6 were merged and categories 3, 4 , 5 and 7 were regarded as incorrect.

casos.clinica:
Excision of lesion urethral meatus. Immuno: HMB-45 strongly positive, NKI/C3 & S100 focally positive, Melan A focally strong positive.
Specimen: Biopsy from urethra (meatus).
Macro: Darkly pigmented nodule of skin measuring 8x7x4mm.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a straight forward case of urethral malignant melanoma. Category 2 suggesting metastatic malignant melanoma was felt to merit half marks, given that there was junctional activity indicating this was the likely primary site. No further clinical information was available on this case.

casos.clinica:
Right kidney space occupying lesion. Immuno: tumour cells strongly positive CD10, cytokeratin (Cam 5.2), CK7, CK19 (patchy) and vimentin (patchy). High mol weight CK (34BE12) is negative.
Specimen: Nephron sparing surgical excision of renal tumour. Macro: Renal parenchyma measuring 40x30x15mm bearing a nodular tumour mass measuring 50x45x30mm with attached fibrofatty tissue measuring 90x30x10mm free of tumour. Weighs 92 grams. On slicing the tumour has pale yellow brown friable cut surface with areas of necrosis and haemorrhage. The capsule overlying the tumour is thin but appears intact. The nearest renal parencymal margin is 5mm from the tumour.
casos.diagnostico: Papillary renal cell carcinoma Type B (columnar cell type)
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a straight forward case of papillary renal cell carcinoma with the majority of participants favouring Eble type II. It was agreed to merge categories 1 and 2, as papillary renal cell carcinoma. The meeting consensus was that responses 3 to 8 should be regarded as incorrect for scoring purposes.

casos.clinica:
FOR EDUCATION AND INTEREST ONLY. Biopsy of bladder base, and red area ?CIS. H/o Gleason 4+5. Metastic prostate ca, ESRF on dialysis. Immuno: strongly positive - PSA, AMACR and CD57. Negative - thrombomodulin, P63, 34BE12,CK5/6, CK7 and CK20.
Specimen: TURBT. Macro: Multiple pieces of pale tan and white tissue, together measuring 2.5x2.0x0. 4cm. Some of the pieces appear to be quite fragile. All embedded.
casos.diagnostico: Papillary TCC G2/3 pT1 and adenocarcinoma of prostate gland invading detrusor and lamina propria.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case was for education and interest only and was not formally discussed. It was reported as mixed papillary TCC and adenocarcinoma of the prostate. It was ascertained from the submitting Pathologist that there was a history of previous hormonal therapy, as suggested by a large number of respondents.

casos.clinica: Bladder tumour in posterior wall. Specimen: Not specified. Macro: 2grams of firm tissue chippings.
casos.diagnostico: G3 pTa micropapillary variant of TCC
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case requested both morphological diagnosis and stage and had to be excluded for scoring purposes due to lack of consensus. Only around 40% of respondents recognized this to be the micropapillary variant of transitional cell carcinoma. Of those that did, a small number commented on the need for a re-resection due to the possibility of up-staging. Non-invasive pTa disease was the favored stage, although a minority of participants suggested focal early lamina propria invasion. The difficulty for the organiser using the ten diagnostic category fields in OMNIS, when multiple diagnostic features were required was emphasized.

casos.clinica: Right renal tumour on CT. Specimen: Right kidney. Macro: Right kidney with a soft white tumour measuring 1.2x1x1cm in the upper pole towards the hilum.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a straightforward case of a triphasic angiomyolipoma. It was agreed to merge categories 1 and 2, as the latter was suspected to be a typographical error. 3 and 4 (spindle cell renal cell carcinoma and spindle cell sarcoma, respectively) were offered as differentials and regarded as incorrect for scoring purposes.

casos.clinica:
TCC ureter and non-functioning kidney removed.
Specimen: Nephro-Ureterectomy. Macro: Ureter expanded by tumour (TCC). Non-functioning kidney contains an incidental yellow/brown nodule in lower pole. 6mm in diameter.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
Although this case surpassed the 70% agreement threshold, there was clearly some confusion in terminology, due to the presence of a clear cell as well as papillary component to the tumour. A small number of participants used the term papillary carcinoma without specifying type i.e. renal cell or transitional. It was pointed out that due to the wide range of diagnoses proffered, category 7 others: included diagnostic entities which were not necessarily equivalent. It was therefore agreed to exclude this case of type II papillary renal cell carcinoma from scoring.

casos.clinica: Known bladder cancer, upper tract imaging shows filling defect in upper calyx. Specimen: Nephro-Uretectomy. Macro: Nephro-uretectomy specimen which on section revealed a friable pale tumour in the collecting system with ?extention into the renal parenchyma.
casos.diagnostico: High grade(grade 3) urothelial carcinoma with renal parenchymal involvement, stage pT3
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case requested morphological diagnosis and stage. It was a straightforward case of papillary and infiltrative transitional cell carcinoma of the renal pelvis, correctly identified by the majority of participants. There was high agreement (87%) that there was renal parenchymal invasion equating to stage pT3 disease. Several participants noted renal tumour carryover on the edge of the section, which may have accounted for a small number suggesting stage pT4. Categories 5, 6 and 8 (pT3/4, pT2 +/- at least ? pT3 and pT3b, respectively) were felt to merit half marks and categories 2, 3, 4, 9 and 10 were regarded as incorrect for scoring.

casos.clinica: Polyp at level of the ejaculatory duct. Specimen: Prostatic urethral polyp. Macro: Multiple pieces of tissue up to 18mm.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
There was good agreement this was an inverted urothelial papilloma (96% agreement). Categories 3 and 5 were felt to merit half marks. Categories 2 and 6 were regarded as incorrect for scoring, as was category 4 (inverted transitional cell neoplasm), which the meeting felt was too imprecise.

casos.clinica: Routine TURP. Immuno: Positive- AE1/3, CD56, Chromogranin, Ki67 approx 100%. Negative- PSA, PAP, CK7/20, TTF-1, LCA, CD20, CD3. Specimen: TURP. Macro: 33g of chippings.
casos.diagnostico: Primary prostatic neuroendocrine carcinoma / small cell
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case generated good agreement that it represented high grade neuroendocrine carcinoma, with a majority favouring primary prostatic origin, although it was emphasized that this diagnosis required clinical and radiological correlation. There was however a wide range of morphological cell types offered. Small cell neuroendrine carcinoma was marginally most popular, but some participants favoured combined small and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma and others large cell neuroendrine carcinoma. It was agreed to merge categories 1, 2, 4 and 5, giving 98% agreement. The meeting felt that category 6 (low grade neuroendocrine carcinoma) was incorrect as this was clearly a high grade tumour, evidenced by coagulative necrosis and high mitotic rate and this diagnosis could negatively influence clinical management. Categories 7, 8, 9 and 10 were also regarded as incorrect for scoring.

casos.clinica:
Bladder tumour. Immuno: Spindle cells are positive for p63 and focally positive for alpha-SMA. They are negative for MNF116, AE1/3, 34βE12, CK7, CK20, S100, desmin, myogenin and h-caldesmon. Multinucleate giant cells are positive for CD68. hCG is negative. Surface epithelial elements positive for p63 and cytokeratins.
Specimen: TURBT. Macro: Multiple chippings.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a case of sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma. It was agreed to merge categories 1 and 3 (sarcomatoid TCC +/- heterologous diff and sarcomatoid Ca or carcinosarcoma +/- heterologous diff, respectively) as equivalent entities, giving good agreement (86%). Categories 2 and 4 which identified TCC without noting the sarcomatoid component were deemed to merit half marks. Categories 5 to 9, which failed to recognize the epithelial nature of the tumour were regarded as incorrect. Category 10 was translated at the meeting as the old terminology for sarcomatoid TCC and has therefore also been merged with 1 and 3 for scoring purposes, although it was felt by the meeting that this terminology was outdated and should be discouraged.

casos.clinica:
Right nephrectomy 2 years ago for Fuhrman2, clear cell renal cell carcinoma, stage pT3b. Follow up scan revealed three discrete lesions in pancreas (one in head, one in body and third in tail).
Specimen: Pancreatic resection. Macro: Total pancrectomy, and attached 55mm loop of duodenum. On serial sectioning of pancreas three discrete nodules up to 21mm in maximum. Each having a variegated cut surface with areas of haemorrhage and tan tumour.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case was also for Education and Interest only and was a case of metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma to the pancreas. Several participants raised the possibility of VHL in this setting.

casos.clinica: Right nephroureterectomy with retrocaval lymph node. Specimen: Kidney. Macro: Upper pole multicystic lesion 50 mm in maximum dimension.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a case of adult cystic nephroma. It was agreed that renal epithelial tumour (REST) and mixed epithelial stromal tumour (MEST) were similar entities and reference was made to a relevant publication (Am J Surg Pathol Vol 31 No 4 April 2007). Accordingly, it was agreed to merge categories 1, 2 & 3 which resulted in a high level of concordance (94%). The age and the sex of the patient had been omitted (in error), from the clinical details on the response form (although these were provided by the submitting Pathologist) and had been commented on by a significant number of participants. For this reason it was decided to allow half marks for cystic partially differentiated nephroma, although it was pointed out that the presence of background arteriosclerosis suggested this was an adult kidney. Following this case it was indicated that there had been a change in practice when preparing the response sheet, so that the Organiser was now given a paper copy of the original case submission form, filled in by the submitting Pathologist (minus the submitting Pathologist's diagnosis), so that this could be checked against the details entered on the response form by the scheme Secretary. Categories 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 & 10 were all regarded by the meeting as incorrect for scoring.

casos.clinica: Incidental bilateral renal tumour. Excision of left 6 cm lower pole tumour. Specimen: Partial nephrectomy. Macro: Partial nephrectomy with a tumour 60 x 50 x 40 mm, partially attached to perinephric fat. The tumour is yellowish-brown with areas of haemorrhagic necrosis.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case of chromophobe carcinoma did not reach the necessary 70% level of agreement required for scoring and was therefore excluded. A significant number of Participants who favoured clear cell RCC, asked for immuno confirmation. The submitting Pathologist did not provide immuno, although it later became clear this had been performed at the time of initial diagnosis. It was emphasised to the meeting the importance; when submitting a case, of providing all the clinical information and additional studies available at the time of the primary diagnosis.

casos.clinica: Raised haemorrhagic lesion. Previous biopsy - foreign body giant cell reaction. Specimen: Bladder biopsies. Macro: Irregular fragments of tissue up to 8 mm in diameter. Immuno: Immuno staining of the amyloid deposits was performed using monospecific antibodies reactive with serum amyloid A protein (SAA), apoliprotein A1 (apoA1) and with Kappa and Lambda immunoglobulin light chains.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case was a straight forward case of bladder amyloid. A number of people commented that the results of the immuno staining were not provided on the response form, which again had been a secretarial omission. As this may have caused some uncertainty it was the meeting consensus that categories 1 & 2 should be merged. Category 3 correctly identified amyloid but made also made the diagnosis of myeloma, which the meeting felt was incorrect on the basis of the information available and could potentially lead to inappropriate clinical management, this was therefore awarded half marks. Category 4, sclerosing haemangioma was regarded as incorrect.

casos.clinica: Grade 3 papillary urothelial carcinoma of the bladder. Specimen: Prostate chips. Macro: Multiple prostate chips weighing less than 2 grams.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case was correctly identified as urothelial carcinoma in situ involving the prostatic urethra and prostatic ducts by 86% of participants. It was agreed to merge categories 3, 5 and 6 which had diagnosed high grade TCC (as well as or rather than CIS) as this was likely to result in similar clinical management. Categories 2, 8 and 10 which proferred, or were suspicious of urothelial dysplasia or TCC were felt to merit half marks and the remaining categories, that offered various benign diagnoses were regarded as incorrect.

casos.clinica: Mass lesion in bladder around left ureteric orifice. Feels prostatic rather than TCC, though separate from prostate anatomically. Specimen: TURBT. Macro: 1 gram of brown coloured tissue chippings. Immuno: Positive CK7, CK20. Negative PSAg PSAP
casos.diagnostico: Invasive TCC G3; pT2 (at least) with CIS
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This TURBT case had requested morphological diagnosis and stage on the response form. It was correctly identified as muscle invasive TCC (stage pT2 at least) by a high proportion of participants (94%), most of whom had also graded it as high grade/grade 3. It was agreed to merge categories 1 & 2 for scoring. Category 4 which correctly identified the tumour to be muscle invasive but queried stage pT3 due to fat invasion and category 10 which also favoured pT3 were felt to merit half marks (it should noted that fat can be present within detrusor muscle and/or the lamina propria and therefore does not necessarily equate to stage pT3 in this type of specimen). Category 7 correctly staged the tumour but offered clear cell carcinoma rather than TCC as the morphological diagnosis and was also felt by consensus to merit half marks. Categories 3, 5, 6, 8 & 9 were regarded as incorrect.

casos.clinica: Frank haematuria, new bladder tumour. Specimen: Bladder tumour resection. Macro: Multiple papillary tan fragments filling 3 cassettes.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case highlighted the problems with inverted growth pattern TCC and the question specifically asked for a stage. As a result answers without a stage scored no points. This pattern of growth shows no definite invasion and was thought by the group to represent pTa and not invasion. As a result categories 1,2 and 6 were merged and category 9 was thought to be cautious and scored �. All other categories suggesting invasion scored 0. It was noted that most contributors offered a grade and most used the 1973 WHO alone.

casos.clinica:
Right Renal Tumour. Specimen: Right Nephrectomy.
Macro: Right kidney covered in fat 220x120x110 mm with attached ureter 100 mm in length. The kidney measures 120x60x60 mm. A well circumscribed brownish tumour measuring 35mm in diameter is present in the mid-pole showing a central scar. The pelvicalyceal system, renal vessels at hilum are unremarkable.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was an oncocytoma and there proved to be nearly complete agreement.

casos.clinica:
Haematuria, smoker, irregular bladder base with oedema and ? submucosal tumour ? prostatitis.
Specimen: Bladder biopsy/resection. Macro: 3 grams pink chippings.
casos.diagnostico: Heavy mixed inflammation with foreign body material ?colovesical fistula
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case showed a fragment of vegetable matter in association with heavily inflamed bladder mucosa. The patient had a fistula confirmed following this TURBT. Less than 70% mentioned the possibility of a colovesical fistula and as a result this was not scorable. Although most identified the foreign material some answered that they thought it was a parasite.

casos.clinica: Tissue said to have been passed in urine followed by haematuria. Specimen: Tissue said to have been passed in urine. Macro: Irregular creamy white piece of tissue measuring 27 x 14 x 5 mm.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was an inverted papilloma and there was near 98% agreement with this. Categories 2,3 and 4 which suggested low grade TCC scored 0.

casos.clinica: Acute presentation left renal tumour. Specimen: Left nephrectomy. Macro: Dark brown tumour in lower pole, 60 x 60 mm. Extensive necrosis and haemorrhage. Focally infiltrates perinephric fat. Immuno: Strong membranous staining for CK7. Focal staining with CD10. Negative for vimentin and CD117.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a chromophobe carcinoma but as opposed to G78 the immunoprofile was given and this was scoreable as a result with 96% stating this. All other answers were deemed incorrect.

casos.clinica: Left Kidney renal mass. Specimen: Left Kidney. Macro: Tumour 5.5cm in mid-part of kidney.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a good example of a metanephric adenoma � though no immunohistochemistry was performed originally this was done as a result of the EQA and this was confirmed. 86% stated this. Although some placed a solid variant of papillary RCC in their differential diagnosis the audience felt this was not correct. The tumour did have fibrous bands and as a result metanephric adenofibroma was also allowed. There were several confused terms given (eg metanephric carcinoma) and it would always seem prudent to check with the WHO classification that the entity exists.

casos.clinica: Renal u/s performed for microscopic haematuria showed a 2.3cm lesion in the interpolar region of the left kidney. On CT scan shown to be solid and enhancing. Nephrectomy performed. Immuno: Positive - CK7 EMA CD57 racemase. Negative - WT1. Ki67- low proliferation rate. Specimen: Nephrectomy Specimen. Macro: Well circumscribed creamy white tumour 26mm in max dimension. Confined to the kidney. Background renal tissue appeared normal.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case proved to be difficult and was excluded from scoring due to lack of consensus. The solid variant of type I papillary RCC (PRCC) was favoured by respondents (59%), but a significant proportion (38%) favoured metanephric adenoma (MA), which was also the diagnosis of the submitting Pathologist (who had actually referred the case for 2nd opinion). The unusual immunoprofile caused some confusion and was commented on by a large number of respondents (CK7, AMACR +ve and WT-1 ?ve favouring PRCC and CD57 +ve favouring MA). A slide was presented highlighting the potential for overlap between these entities immunohistochemically and it was felt that molecular analysis was required for definitive diagnosis (the trisomy of 7 and 17 and loss of Y typical of most papillary RCC's not being a feature of MA). This has been relayed back to the submitting Pathologist and it was indicated that the molecular results could be circulated to participants in due course for educational purposes.

casos.clinica:
Right ureteric tumour. Nephro-ureterectomy done.
Specimen: Ureter. Macro: A fragmented kidney with 160mm length of ureter. The ureter shows a nodular tumour in the lumen and infiltrating the wall measuring 8x6mm situated 80mm from the distal end.
casos.diagnostico: Invasive high grade (G3) transitional cell carcinoma
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a case of invasive high grade (G3) transitional cell carcinoma, which morphologically was recognized correctly by all respondents. The response form also asked for stage to be provided. There was high agreement (82%) for pT3 disease and category 3 (stage pT3a) was merged for scoring purposes, although it was noted that substaging (pT3a & pT3b) only pertains to bladder tumours in the TNM classification. Because there was only early extension beyond the muscularis propria, on a show of hands the meeting felt that stage pT2 should be awarded half marks. Stage pT4 and no stage provided were regarded as incorrect.

casos.clinica: Incidental upper pole renal mass with suspicious features. Specimen: Partial nephrectomy. Macro: 4cm multiloculated cystic tumour.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a case of a cystic/multicystic clear cell renal carcinoma where a significant number of respondents (53%) favoured a diagnosis of multilocular cystic (clear cell) renal cell carcinoma (MLCRCC). The strict diagnostic criteria for MLCRCC (purely cystic without expansile nodules) were emphasized and for scoring purposes the meeting favoured merging categories 1,2 & 3 (clear cell RCC +/- cystic multicystic, MLCRCC and Multi/cystic renal cell carcinoma, respectively). Categories 4-6 (Angiomyolipoma, myxoid liposarcoma, Lymphangioma +/- ossifying, ossifying haemangioma, myelolipoma and others: Hamartoma, juxtaglomerular cell tumour and myxoma, respectively) were regarded as incorrect.

casos.clinica: History of haematuria. At cytoscopy irregular mucosa & ? very superficial papillary TCC. Specimen: Bladder tumour. Macro: Multiple fragments, 1cc in aggregate.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This case requested both morphological diagnosis and stage and was correctly identified as a papillary transitional cell carcinoma by all respondents, although one person had mentioned transitional papilloma as a differential diagnosis. There was high agreement (92%) that this was non-invasive, stage pTa. A small number of people had commented on assessment of possible lamina propria invasion being difficult due to diathermy artifact, but it was emphasized that there was no stromal desmoplasia or retraction artefact to suggest invasion. Category 2 (TCC pTa + CIS) was; on a show of hands, felt to merit half marks as the diagnosis of CIS could have significant implications for clinical management and categories 4 & 5 (stage pT2 and pT1, respectively), which had diagnosed definite invasion were regarded incorrect. Categories 6 & 7 (?pT1 and suspicious of pT1, respectively) which had suggested possible lamina propria invasion were deemed to merit half marks.

casos.clinica: CT scan shows a right renal mass. Immuno: Diffuse strong positivity for AE1/AE3, Racemace, CK7 and E-Cadherin. Patchy positivity for CD15, and negative for CD10 and RCC. Specimen: Right radical nephrectomy. Macro: Right kidney 150x75x60mm with ureter measuring. The upper pole has a spherical tumour 65mm confined to the kidney. The pelvi-calyceal system renal vessels at hilum are unremarkable.
casos.diagnostico: Renal carcinoma (papillary RCC versus mucinous tubular and spindle cell carcinoma)
casos.comentario:
NOT SCORED
Meeting comments:
This case was also excluded from scoring due to lack of consensus. Most respondents (65%) favoured papillary RCC (PRCC) (which was also the diagnosis of the submitting Pathologist). However, a significant number (30%) favoured mucinous tubular and spindle cell carcinoma (MTSCC) and some people had commented on the presence of stromal mucin and suggested an ABPAS stain. This was relayed to the submitting Pathologist, who subsequently performed an ABPAS stain, which was positive. The focal low grade spindle morphology and stromal mucin would both favour MTSCC over PRCC. It was emphasized that there is considerable immunohistochemical overlap between these entities and that in difficult cases molecular analysis is required to make the distinction. Feedback to be given to the submitting Pathologist.

casos.clinica:
History of melanoma removed from right shoulder 2 years previously. Presented recently with haematuria. Cytoscopy showed 3cm melanotic solid tumour on posterior and right lateral bladder wall. TURBT and cold cup biopsy of tumour base. Immuno: Strongly positive for Melan-A, NK1C3, S100 protein and HMB45 (patchy). Labelling for high mol. Wt cytokeratin (34BE12), CK7 and CK20 is negative.
Specimen: Bladder tumour, TURBT specimen. Macro: Multiple pieces of grey brown tissue weighing 5grams.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a straightforward case of malignant melanoma involving the bladder. On the basis of the clinical history of a previous cutaneous melanoma most people favoured metastatic melanoma. It was agreed to merge categories 1,2 & 3 for scoring purposes giving 100% agreement.

casos.clinica: History of large 'abdominal' mass detected on routine clinical examination. Biopsy suggestive of renal cell carcinoma. Subsequent left radical nephrectomy with part of colon, pancreas and spleen removed. Immuno: CD117, CD10 and CK7 positive. Variably positive for AE1/3. Focal vimentin positive. Negative staining for Melan A, Inhibin, CK20 and chromogranin. Specimen: Left nephrectomy. Macro: Left kidney with tumour measuring 16x17.5x14cm. The tumour has a nodular grey homogenous cut surface with small areas of haemorrhage. The tumour has largely replaced the kidney. The renal sinus contains tumour. The mass was also adherent to part of the colon and pancreas removed in one area.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
There was very high agreement (99%) this was a chromophobe renal cell carcinoma, which was the diagnosis of the submitting Pathologist. Categories 2 & 3 (clear cell RCC and renal cell carcinoma, respectively), were regarded incorrect.

casos.clinica: Right nephrectomy for tumour. Specimen: Right nephrectomy. Macro: Right kidney and perinephric fat weighing 460g. Kidney measures 110mm pole to pole. In the upper mid zone on the anterior surface there is a tumour nodule 3.2mm in diameter. This has a haemorrhagic microcystic appearance.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
This was a case of renal oncocytoma, correctly diagnosed by 90% of respondents, with a prominent microcystic architecture, which is an acceptable morphological feature. After some discussion it was agreed the diagnosis was tenable on morphological grounds and that categories 8 & 9 (tubulocystic neoplasm carcinoma vs oncocytoma and oncocytic/eosinophilic renal tumour needs immuno, respectively), merited half marks. Categories 2-7 (renal cell carcinoma +/- oncocytic/eosinophilic/granular, tubulocystic carcinoma, oncocytosis, clear cell RCC +/- granular and cystic nephroma, respectively) were regarded incorrect.

casos.clinica: Resection of bladder tumour on the dome. Cold cup biopsies. Specimen: Bladder biopsy, bladder mass. Macro: Tissue weighing <1g.
casos.comentario:
Meeting comments:
There was insufficient agreement for this case to be scored as there was split opinion as to whether there was invasion or not. A fragment with diathermy artefact with glands within it was present but the consensus at the meeting that this was subjective. Clearly the advice for the clinicians was for further tissue to confirm this, though 32% of replies felt that there was enough to call invasive on this biopsy alone. There were comments that this may have represented metastatic adenocarcinoma, though the immunoprofile given would favour a bladder primary as the tumour was CK20 positive. No definite urothelial component was identified and there were no features of nephrogenic metaplasia. The submitting pathologist had reported this as villous adenoma but no further follow up was available.

casos.clinica: Previous G2 pTa TCC. Past BCG. Recurrence TURT done. Specimen: TURT. Macro: N/A.
casos.comentario: The consensus at the meeting was that this represented a sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma. This was stated by 79.5% of respondents. Spindle cell carcinoma was felt to be not totally incorrect and the consensus was that this should receive half marks. The other diagnoses either made no mention of the sarcomatous stroma or called it benign and were deemed incorrect.

casos.clinica: New bladder tumour, solid ?incomplete re-section. Immuno: None performed. Specimen: Bladder chippings. Macro: 3 grams of cream coloured chippings overall measuring 30x35mm all embedded in two cassettes.
casos.diagnostico: Carcinoma (urothelial carcinoma with squamous differention +/- lymphoepitheiial, poorly differentiated tumour with squamous differentiation, squamous cell carcinoma and lymphoepithelial SCC)
casos.comentario: Although this tumour had a combination of various differentiations it was felt that it could be scored. There was a large squamous component as well as a lymphoepithelial component but a small area of possible urothelial differentiation was also present. The consensus was that urothelial carcinoma with squamous differention +/- lymphoepitheiial, poorly differentiated tumour with squamous differentiation, squamous cell carcinoma and lymphoepithelial SCC were considered correct. Urothelial carcinoma alone and lymphoepithelial urothelial carcinoma both scored half marks as there was no mention of the squamous component (though it should be noted that the submitting pathologist had not put this in the diagnosis given either). Poorly differentiated tumour with a broad differential was deemed incorrect as it was too vague. The other diagnoses (basaloid SCC, SCC with sarcomatoid areas, adenocarcinoma with spindle cell nodule) were considered as incorrect.

casos.clinica:
Presented with a bladder mass ?endometriosis.
Specimen: Bladder chippings. Macro: Bladder chippings measuring 15x15x5mm.
casos.comentario: This biopsy had areas of endometriosis and cystitis cystica. Some pathologists noted the presence of glandular structures with ciliated epithelium and considered this as mullerianosis/endosalpingiosis. For scoring purposes endometriosis, mullerianosis, and endosalpingiosis were considered correct (diagnoses 1,2,5,6,7). There was no evidence of CIS or dysplasia in the endometriosis and these diagnoses (3,4) were considered as incorrect.

casos.clinica: Haematuria. Solid red/sandy patches in bladder at cytoscopy. Specimen: TURBT. Macro: Fragments of tissue 25mm x 25mm in aggregate.
casos.comentario: This was a straightforward case of schistosomiasis and all diagnoses given were considered correct and merged.

casos.clinica:
C/o Haematuria. Solid bladder tumour. ** Please provide morphological diagnosis and stage **.
Specimen: Bladder (cystectomy). Macro: Cystectomy measuring 110x110x50mm containing a friable greyish white exophtic tumour measuring 60x45x40mm on the posterior, left lateral and anterior walls.
casos.comentario: Participants were asked for the morphological diagnosis and the stage. The meeting felt that a half mark could be assigned to each of these components. The diagnosis squamous cell carcinoma pT3 or pT3a was stated by 85% of participants (diagnosis 1 and 4) and this was considered correct as splitting of pT3 could not be done as the macroscopic description did not state whether the tumour was outside the bladder. The diagnoses of SCC but pT2 or pT2b or pT2a at least or sitting on fence pT2b/pT3a (diagnosis 2,3,8,9) were considered as half marks as the stage was incorrect. Those stating no stage but SCC also received half marks. No urothelial component was identified on the section and as a result urothelial carcinoma with squamous differentiation but staged correctly received half marks. Verrucous SCC with no stage was regarded incorrect.

casos.clinica: Right nephrectomy. Specimen: Kidney tumour. Macro: 54mm cream coloured and focally haemorrhagic.
casos.comentario: Over 98% stated this was papillary renal cell carcinoma with the majority of those stating the subtype as type 1. This was called correct, all other diagnoses were considered as incorrect for scoring (clear cell, chromophobe, translocation associated, mixed papillary and collecting duct, mucinous tubular and spindle cell carcinoma).

casos.clinica: Mass at dome of bladder: resected.
casos.comentario:
Average 2.6/5
This case was set to explore the ability of candidates to assess a paediatric neoplasm arising in an unusual location. Recognising that few candidates would have had significant experience in paediatric pathology the marking scheme was lenient.
Pass marks were given to candidates offering a sensible differential diagnosis of paediatric small round cell neoplasms (neuroblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, Ewing's tumour, PNET, lymphoblastic lymphoma and Wilm's tumour|) and indicating an awareness of the need for immunohistochemical staining and specialist referral.
Additional marks were awarded to candidates suggesting appropriate immunohistochemistry (NB84/ PGP 9.5, synaptophysin, chromogranin, CD99, desmin, MyoD1 and CD4) and indicating the need for genetic studies to include investigation of MYCN, and the awareness of the prognostic importance of n-myc oncogene amplification.
Borderline fails were awarded for poor and incomplete lists of differential diagnoses and confident diagnosis of small round blue cell neoplasms other than neuroblastoma. Benign diagnoses and confident diagnoses of malignant tumours other than those listed above were regarded as clear fails.
Most candidates answered this question well, with a sensible list of differential diagnoses. Many added considerable value to their answers. Just under a quarter failed, for the reasons indicated above.

casos.clinica: Lower urinary tract symptoms. Abnormal bladder mucosa found at cystoscopy. Multiple biopsies.
casos.comentario:
Average: 2.46/5
This case aimed to assess the ability of candidates to diagnose a well-recognised benign bladder lesion that is sometimes over diagnosed as malignancy.
Candidates offering a basic description and a correct diagnosis of nephrogenic metaplasia (nephrogenic adenoma) were given a pass mark. Additional marks were given to candidates aware of the aetiology of the condition (inflammatory genitourinary conditions, bladder instrumentation), male predominance and the limited utility of immunohistochemical staining. Some candidates suggested immunohistochemistry and special stains to exclude prostatic carcinoma and clear cell adenocarcinoma: appropriate special stains were awarded extra marks.
Differential diagnoses which included nephrogenic adenoma but did not favour the diagnosis were given borderline fail marks, as were answers indicating a benign lesion, but failing to name the lesion. Candidates offering definite diagnoses of malignancy or favouring malignant diagnoses were given clear fails.
Most candidates offered good answers to this question, often with considerable added value. A small but appreciable proportion offered equivocal or indefinite diagnoses and a few candidates made inappropriate diagnoses of malignancy.

casos.clinica: Lesion 45mm diameter, left kidney. Left partial nephrectomy.
casos.comentario:
Average: 2.66/5
This case considered a well-recognised subtype of renal cell carcinoma which requires distinction from renal cell carcinoma NOS. Candidates able to describe the lesion and favour a diagnosis of chromophobe renal cell carcinoma were awarded pass marks. Additional marks were given to candidates suggesting appropriate immunohistochemical and other stains (Hale�s colloidal iron, CD10, CK7, vimentin) to allow distinction from renal cell carcinoma NOS and oncocytoma. Awareness of better prognosis compared with renal cell carcinoma NOS also gained higher marks.
Candidates favouring a diagnosis of renal cell carcinoma NOS were given borderline fails. A clear fail would have been awarded to any candidate favouring a benign diagnosis.
Most candidates answered this question well, and many candidates added considerable value. A minority of candidates offered equivocal diagnoses or favoured renal cell carcinoma NOS.

casos.clinica: Right orchidectomy for testicular lesion. Right testis.
casos.comentario:
Average score 2.87/5
This was a good example of a pure yolk sac tumour. The case aimed to assess candidates' knowledge of testicular tumours, and their capacity to describe these lesions and suggest appropriate ancillary investigations.
Candidates answered this question very well, with only just over 20% suffering marginal fails. A pass mark was given for a competent description and a confident diagnosis of yolk sac tumour. Additional marks were given for appropriate immunohistochemistry, better than average description, knowledge of epidemiology and understanding of favourable prognosis given appropriate diagnosis and treatment, as well as understanding the need to seek correlation with biochemical investigations. Borderline fails were awarded to candidates who inappropriately recognised other forms of testicular tumour, or lacked confidence by resorting to differential diagnoses. Some candidates preferred a diagnosis of mixed germ cell tumour.

casos.clinica: Large calculus, right renal pelvis. Atrophic right kidney. Right simple nephrectomy.
casos.comentario:
Average 2.51
This case sought to assess the ability of candidates to assess a specific pattern of inflammation in a resected kidney. Candidates were given a very helpful history.
Pass marks were awarded to candidates able to describe the lesion and the pattern of inflammation and arrive at a diagnosis of a benign inflammatory condition, preferably naming the lesion as xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis. Additional marks were given to candidates offering accurate comments regarding aetiology, and proffering better than average descriptions.
Borderline fails were given to candidates observing other specific forms of inflammation (eg- granulomatous inflammation). Malignant/neoplastic diagnoses were given clear fails.
The great majority of candidates answered this question well, and many added considerable value to their answers. A surprising number of candidates mistook the inflammatory lesion for an angiomyolipoma, and a few significantly overcalled this inflammatory lesion, finding evidence of renal cell carcinoma. Surprisingly, some candidates found evidence of endometriosis.

casos.clinica: Bladder biopsies
Tumour in kidney
Haematuria. Needle core biopsy of mass left loin.
casos.comentario:

To gain a pass mark candidates had to provide an adequate description and arrive at the correct diagnosis or a differential diagnosis favouring the correct diagnosis.
Additional marks were given to candidates suggesting appropriate immunohistochemistry to confirm, and indicating a knowledge of Fuhrman grading. Borderline fails were awarded to candidates whose answers lacked confidence or precision.
Most candidates answered this question very well, with a majority adding some value to their answers.
